Know your Voting Options
There are three voting options in North Carolina from which a voter who is eligible to vote in the 2026 General Election may choose to cast their ballot:
1) Absentee-By-Mail Voting
This method of voting requires registered voters to request a ballot through the new online
Absentee Request Portal (link)
on the NC State Board of Elections website or complete and submit the
North Carolina Absentee Ballot Request Form (PDF)
to the New Hanover County Board of Elections Office.
The deadline to request an Absentee-by-Mail ballot is Tuesday, October 20, 2026, at 5 pm.
Once the request form has been processed, you will receive your absentee ballot in the mail to complete and return by hand or by mail prior to the Absentee Ballot Return Deadline (Tuesday, November 3, 2026, by 7:30 PM). A reason is not required to vote using this method and your ballot may be mailed anywhere in the world.
Please visit our
Absentee Voting page (link)
for more information on voting Absentee-By-Mail.
2) Early Voting
Early Voting allows you to cast an in-person ballot during the 17 days before Election Day. Early Voting gives you the flexibility to choose when and where you vote and typically offers shorter lines and a quicker voting experience than on Election Day.
Visit our
Early Voting page (link)
to learn more about Early Voting and find your closest Early Voting location (link).
3) Election Day Voting
The most traditional method of voting is on Election Day. All of the county's 41 precincts will be open on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, for Election Day Voting. All precincts will be open 6:30 AM - 7:30 PM!
Election Day is the last chance that a person has to vote in the election. If you choose to vote on Election Day, you should present at the polling place that is specific to your voting precinct as noted on your voter registration record.
Visit our
Polling Places page (link)
to find out where you should vote on Election Day
Provisional Voting
Provisional Voting is a fail-safe voting method that is available to any voter during Early Voting and on Election Day when there is a question of that person's eligibility to vote. For more information about provisional voting in North Carolina please visit the
North Carolina State Board of Elections website (link)
.
Sample Ballots
For most elections, the ballot received when you vote is determined based on the jurisdictional information that corresponds with your residential address. To determine the ballot style(s) on which you may be eligible to vote in future elections, visit the
NC State Board of Elections Voter Search Tool (Link)
!
If you are printing your sample ballot, you may need to select ‘Fit to Printable Area’ or ‘Fit’ in the printer settings in order to scale it correctly to standard letter-size paper. Due to the length of the ballot, the sample ballot files are in a longer paper-size format. Sample ballots are also available at our office.

Check Your Voter Registration Status
Before voting in any election, it is important to confirm that you are a registered voter and that your voter registration contains all of your most recent information.
Your voter registration record should accurately reflect the following to ensure a quick and efficient Election Day experience:
your full name,
address,
and party affiliation.
Check the status of your voter registration (link)
!
Verify Your Polling Place
If you plan to vote during the Early Voting period, you can present to vote at any of the Early Voting sites around New Hanover County no matter where in the county you are registered to vote. Visit our
Early Voting page (link)
for more details.
If you plan to vote on Election Day, you must present to vote in the precinct in which you are registered. If you present to vote at any precinct other than your own, you will be directed to your correct polling place or be given the opportunity to vote a provisional ballot, which may slow your Election Day experience.
Visit our
Polling Places page (link)
to find out where you should vote on Election Day. Polls are open on Election Day from 6:30 am to 7:30 pm.

Closing of Early Voting Equipment
As required by law, at 7:30 PM on November 3, 2026, the New Hanover County Board of Elections will take action to close the voting equipment used during Early Voting. This action will occur in the presence of a bi-partisan team of two county board members.
Voter Photo ID for 2026 General Election
Current Status:
Photo ID Required for Voting
Voters will be asked to show photo ID when voting in North Carolina, starting with the 2023 Municipal Elections. Voters will also be asked to show photo ID in the 2026 General Election.
Voters who vote by mail must include a photocopy of an acceptable ID inside the "photo ID envelope" that comes with their ballot. Or they may complete an ID Exception Form with the absentee ballot return envelope.
Most voters will simply show their driver's license, but many other types of ID will be accepted. For a list of acceptable photo IDs, click the following link to the NC State Board of Elections' website:
Voter ID (link)
.
Voters without a photo ID can get a
No Fee ID Card (link)
from the NCDMV. Voters can also get a free voter ID card from the county board of elections office. Contact the New Hanover County Board of Elections Office at (910) 798-7330 for more information.
For more information about Voter ID in North Carolina visit the
North Carolina State Board of Elections Voter ID webpage (link).
Curbside Voting
By law, every voting site in North Carolina must offer curbside voting for voters who are unable to enter the voting place without physical assistance due to age or disability. Through curbside voting, a voter can cast a ballot while in a vehicle outside the polling location.
Each polling place or early voting site will have clearly identified locations outside the polling place to denote the area used for curbside voting. Curbside voters must sign an affidavit affirming that because of age or physical disability they are unable to enter the voting place without physical assistance to cast their ballot. A curbside voter has the same rights to
voting assistance at voting sites
as any other voter.
